correctness.rationale: Subtraction of one required parity edge at each vertex preserves balance. The augmentation decomposes into simple cycles, and the component-incidence connectivity equivalence follows in both directions from Euler circuits. Every possible simple cycle whose length could occur in an optimal augmentation is exhaustively generated canonically, and integer bitmask dynamic programming finds the minimum connected family. Explicit witnesses meet all upper bounds; the extracted standalone verifier returns VERIFY_OK at orders 2–7 and a separately implemented brute-force small-case checker returns CROSSCHECK_OK at orders 2–4. No inference beyond the verified finite domain.

originality.rationale: The full inspected 2013 weight-range construction handles contiguous weight sets and its Eulerian subgraphs, whereas the even-parity set is a disconnected union of alternating weight levels and shortest completion requires surplus factors. The 2003 pattern-unavoidability paper uses relabeling-pattern equivalence, not exact indexed binary factors. Near-neighbor comparisons in the accessible previous research corpus concern weight two only, Fibonacci restrictions, unoriented covers or universal partial words, none of which logically determines the even-parity minima. No equivalent exact finite table was identified in research-index and primary-literature searches; the thesis full-text limitation and unindexed literature remain disclosed risks.

value.rationale: A natural parity restriction disconnects the otherwise simple binary universal-cycle overlap graph. Exact shortest circular covers give a benchmark beyond existence and generic word counts. After order four requires a complete de Bruijn cycle, the first renewed shortening occurs at order five, and exact odd-only augmentation deficits at n=5 and n=7, show that permitting mixed-parity repeated windows has a structural optimization effect not captured by the standard parity-necklace gluing idea. The general cycle-hypergraph reduction helps explain the obstruction and supports future exact investigations.
